title: Do You Know How to Ask Great Questions?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

sentences.en: Do you know how to ask great questions? A few years ago, back in 2022, I released an episode called How to Ask Better Questions in English.
sentences.zh: 你知道如何提出好问题吗？几年前，也就是2022年，我发布了一期名为《如何在英语中问出更好的问题》的节目。

sentences.en: And today’s episode is an update to that original one.
sentences.zh: 而今天的节目是对当年那期内容的更新。

sentences.en: The core idea is the same, because it’s still important, but a lot has changed since then.
sentences.zh: 核心理念是一样的，因为这依然很重要，但自那以后发生了很多变化。

sentences.en: I’ve changed as a podcaster and an educator, and I think English learners’ needs have changed too.
sentences.zh: 作为播客创作者和教育工作者，我变了，我想英语学习者的需求也变了。

sentences.en: In fact, the way we use English in 2026 is very different from how we used it just a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们在2026年使用英语的方式，与短短几年前相比已经有了很大不同。

sentences.en: We now spend more time in online meetings, working with international teams, and communicating through messages, emails, and AI tools.
sentences.zh: 我们现在花更多的时间在在线会议上，与国际团队合作，并通过消息、电子邮件和AI工具进行沟通。

sentences.en: In this kind of world, the ability to ask good questions matters more than ever.
sentences.zh: 在这样的世界里，提出好问题的能力比以往任何时候都更加重要。

sentences.en: Most people know how to ask questions, but very few people know how to ask good questions.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都知道如何问问题，但极少数人知道如何问出好问题。

sentences.en: And learning how to do that can change your English, your conversations, and the opportunities you have.
sentences.zh: 学会这一点可以改变你的英语水平、你的对话以及你所拥有的机遇。

sentences.en: Today, we will look at different types of question, what makes a good question, and I’ll give you a lot of useful advice!
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨不同类型的问题以及什么构成了一个好问题，同时我也会给你很多实用的建议！

sentences.en: In 2026, I think “question asking,” or “the ability to ask good questions”, is becoming a vital life skill.
sentences.zh: 在2026年，我认为“提问”，或者说“提出好问题的能力”，正在成为一项至关重要的生活技能。

sentences.en: Many people work in global teams. Maybe you sit in online meetings with people you’ve never met in person.
sentences.zh: 很多人都在全球化团队中工作。也许你参加的在线会议里，与会者都是你从未在现实中见过的人。

sentences.en: Or maybe you build professional or personal relationships through messages, emails, and short conversations on Instagram.
sentences.zh: 或者，你可能通过消息、电子邮件以及Instagram上的简短对话建立职业或个人关系。

sentences.en: In all of these situations, asking the right question at the right moment can make a huge difference.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些情况下，在正确的时机提出正确的问题会产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: In a global workplace, for example, good questions help you understand expectations, avoid misunderstandings, and show that you’re engaged.
sentences.zh: 例如，在全球化职场中，好的问题能帮你理解期望、避免误解，并展现出你的投入。

sentences.en: And this is especially important if English isn’t your first language.
sentences.zh: 如果英语不是你的母语，这一点尤为重要。

sentences.en: Online, in meetings or in online classes or online calls with your friends, it’s easy to stay silent or get ignored, so a clear and thoughtful question can really help you understand better and get people to understand you better.
sentences.zh: 在线上，无论是开会、上在线课程还是与朋友进行网络通话，保持沉默或被忽视都很容易，因此一个清晰、周到的问题真的能大有帮助，让你更好地理解他人，也让别人更好地理解你。

sentences.en: This is also true in the age of AI. Whether you are using ChatGPT, or Gemini or Claude or whatever else there is out there right now, the quality of what you get from the AI depends almost entirely on the quality of what you ask.
sentences.zh: 在AI时代同样如此。无论你使用的是ChatGPT、Gemini、Claude还是现有的其他工具，你从AI那里获得的质量几乎完全取决于你提问的质量。

sentences.en: Vague questions lead to vague answers; clear questions lead to useful ones.
sentences.zh: 模糊的问题导致模糊的答案；清晰的问题带来有用的答案。

sentences.en: The skill here is exactly the same. You need to know what you want and you need to express it clearly.
sentences.zh: 这里的核心技能完全一样。你需要知道自己想要什么，并把它清晰地表达出来。

sentences.en: And this isn’t just my opinion. Research consistently shows that people who ask more questions in conversations are seen as more engaged, more intelligent, and more likable.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是我的观点。研究一再表明，在对话中提问更多的人显得更投入、更聪明、也更讨人喜欢。

sentences.en: They also tend to learn more. Asking good questions demonstrates curiosity, confidence, and respect.
sentences.zh: 他们往往也学得更多。提出好问题体现了好奇心、自信和尊重。

sentences.en: These are all qualities that matter in professional and personal relationships.
sentences.zh: 这些都是在职业和个人交往中至关重要的品质。

sentences.en: We live in a world full of information. Answers are everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个信息爆炸的世界里。答案无处不在。

sentences.en: You can Google almost anything, or AI can generate explanations in seconds.
sentences.zh: 你几乎可以谷歌搜索任何东西，或者让AI在几秒钟内生成解释。

sentences.en: But what really matters now, is whether you are asking the “right” questions to get the “right” answers.
sentences.zh: 但现在真正重要的是，你是否在提出“正确”的问题以获得“正确”的答案。

sentences.en: Because if you’re not asking good questions, the information that you get from Google or from Gemini may be incorrect or not exactly what you are hoping for.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你没有问出好问题，你从谷歌或Gemini获得的信息可能是错误的，或者不完全是你所期望的。

sentences.en: Most people are not very good at asking questions.
sentences.zh: 大多数人不怎么擅长提问。

sentences.en: This isn’t an English learner problem. Native speakers are just as bad, maybe worse at asking questions.
sentences.zh: 这不是英语学习者独有的问题。母语者提问水平同样很差，甚至可能更糟。

sentences.en: I’ve probably made mistakes, myself, asking questions.
sentences.zh: 我自己提问时也可能犯过错误。

sentences.en: I’ve sat in university lectures and business meetings where someone asks a question, and halfway through that question, everyone in the room is already confused or bored or frustrated.
sentences.zh: 我曾坐在大学阶梯教室和商务会议中，听到有人提出一个问题，结果问题还没问到一半，屋里的每个人就已经感到困惑、无聊或沮丧了。

sentences.en: One common problem is rambling. Rambling questions.
sentences.zh: 常见的一个问题就是冗长啰嗦。也就是啰里啰嗦的问题。

sentences.en: People talk for so long that by the time they finish, it’s no longer clear what they’re actually asking.
sentences.zh: 人们说得太久，以至于等他们说完时，大家已经听不清他们到底在问什么了。

sentences.en: Sometimes the question includes background information that isn’t necessary.
sentences.zh: 有时问题包含了一些不必要的背景信息。

sentences.en: Sometimes it turns into a speech. And sometimes it never really becomes a question at all.
sentences.zh: 有时它变成了一场演讲。还有的时候，它根本就成不了什么问题。

sentences.en: Another issue is questions designed to show intelligence rather than get an answer.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，有些提问的目的不是为了得到答案，而是为了炫耀智商。

sentences.en: I saw this constantly as a student at university.
sentences.zh: 我在大学当学生时经常看到这种现象。

sentences.en: Someone would ask a long, complex question filled with academic language, because they wanted to sound smart.
sentences.zh: 有人会抛出一个充满学术术语的长而复杂的问题，因为他们想让自己听起来很聪明。

sentences.en: And the result was usually the same. The professor had to ask them to clarify, or the professor answered a completely different question because they were confused.
sentences.zh: 而结果通常都一样。教授不得不让他们解释清楚，或者教授回答了一个完全不相干的问题，因为他们被绕晕了。

sentences.en: Then there are questions with hidden opinions.
sentences.zh: 还有一种是带有隐藏观点的问题。

sentences.en: These are questions that already contain judgment or an assumption.
sentences.zh: 这些问题本身就包含着主观判断或某种假设。

sentences.en: They are biased. They don’t really want an answer.
sentences.zh: 它们带有偏见。提问者其实并不是真的想要答案。

sentences.en: They want agreement, and if the other person disagrees, the conversation can quickly become awkward or defensive.
sentences.zh: 他们想要的是认同，如果对方不同意，对话很快就会变得尴尬或充满防守意味。

sentences.en: This is why question quality matters. A bad question wastes time.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题质量至关重要的原因。一个糟糕的问题纯粹是在浪费时间。

sentences.en: It wastes your time and everyone else’s.
sentences.zh: 它浪费了你的时间，也浪费了其他所有人的时间。

sentences.en: But a good question creates value. It clarifies something.
sentences.zh: 但一个好的问题能创造价值。它能澄清某些事情。

sentences.en: It opens up the conversation. It leads to better understanding and better outcomes, hopefully.
sentences.zh: 它能打开对话。它有望带来更好的理解和更好的结果。

sentences.en: I think we should talk about some of the different types of question.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们应该聊聊几种不同类型的问题。

sentences.en: It’s useful to think about why you are asking a question.
sentences.zh: 思考你为什么要问这个问题是非常有用的。

sentences.en: Different questions serve different purposes, and once you understand that, choosing the right type of question becomes much easier.
sentences.zh: 不同类型的问题服务于不同的目的，一旦你明白了这一点，选择正确类型的问题就会变得容易得多。

sentences.en: I have grouped these questions into different types based on my own opinion, uh, but there are many different ways to do this.
sentences.zh: 我根据我自己的观点，把这些问题分成了不同的类型，嗯，不过也有很多其他不同的分类方法。

sentences.en: The first type I would talk about is “information questions”.
sentences.zh: 我要谈的第一种是“信息类问题”。

sentences.en: Information questions are the most basic and most common type of question.
sentences.zh: 信息类问题是最基础、最常见的一类问题。

sentences.en: The purpose is simple: get information. We can divide these into closed and open questions.
sentences.zh: 目的很简单：获取信息。我们可以把它们分为封闭式问题和开放式问题。

sentences.en: Closed questions usually have one or two possible answers.
sentences.zh: 封闭式问题通常只有一两个可能的答案。

sentences.en: Normally “yes” or “no”. They’re useful when you need something clear and specific.
sentences.zh: 通常是“是”或“否”。当你需要明确且具体的事情时，它们非常有用。

sentences.en: For example: “Did you finish the report?”
sentences.zh: 例如：“你写完报告了吗？”

sentences.en: Or “Is the meeting at 11?” The answers to these questions are either “yes” or “no “.
sentences.zh: 或者“会议是在11点开吗？”这些问题的答案要么是“是”，要么是“否”。

sentences.en: “Yes, I finished a report.” Open questions, on the other hand, invite explanation.
sentences.zh: “是的，我写完报告了。”另一方面，开放式问题则能引发进一步的解释。

sentences.en: They usually begin with “what”, “why “, or “how “.
sentences.zh: 它们通常以“什么”、“为什么”或“如何”开头。

sentences.en: Open questions are far better for learning because they give the other person an opportunity to think or explain something or share information you didn’t even know to ask for.
sentences.zh: 开放式问题对学习要好得多，因为它们给了对方思考、解释某些事情，或者分享你甚至不知道该如何去问的信息的机会。

sentences.en: For example: “Why did you choose to study this subject?”
sentences.zh: 例如：“你为什么选择学这个科目？”

sentences.en: “How does this usually work?” If your goal is understanding, rather than confirmation, open questions are almost always the better choice.
sentences.zh: “这个通常是怎么运作的？”如果你的目标是理解而非确认，开放式问题几乎总是更好的选择。

sentences.en: The next set of question types are best categorized, in my opinion, as direction shaping questions.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，下一组问题类型最好被归类为引导方向类问题。

sentences.en: They influence the direction of a conversation.
sentences.zh: 它们会影响对话的走向。

sentences.en: Probing questions help you go deeper. They’re often used when something isn’t clear or when you want more detail.
sentences.zh: 追问能帮你进行更深入的探讨。当某事不够清晰或者当你想要更多细节时，它们经常被派上用场。

sentences.en: These are especially important for English learners, because they allow you to check meaning without pretending you understand everything.
sentences.zh: 对于英语学习者来说，这类问题尤为重要，因为它们能让你在不假装自己全懂的情况下核实意思。

sentences.en: Examples include: “Could you explain that part in more detail?”
sentences.zh: 例子包括：“你能把那部分详细解释一下吗？”

sentences.en: “When you say it was challenging, what was the hardest part?”
sentences.zh: “当你说是具有挑战性的时候，最难的部分是什么？”

sentences.en: Follow-up questions are a natural extension of this.
sentences.zh: 后续问题（跟进提问）是这种提问的自然延伸。

sentences.en: You ask them after hearing an answer, and they show that you are listening and interested.
sentences.zh: 你在听到答案后顺势追问，这表明你在倾听并且很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Research consistently shows that follow-up questions make conversations more engaging and more cooperative.
sentences.zh: 研究一再表明，追问会让对话变得更引人入胜、更有协作性。

sentences.en: There are also refocusing questions, which are really useful when a discussion goes off track.
sentences.zh: 还有重新聚焦类问题，当讨论偏离正题时，这类问题真的非常有用。

sentences.en: Instead of interrupting or disagreeing directly, a well-timed question can gently bring the conversation back to the main point.
sentences.zh: 与其直接打断或表示反对，一个切入时机恰当的问题可以温和地把对话拉回正题。

sentences.en: “What does this mean for the deadline?” Or “So, what’s the next step from here?”
sentences.zh: “这对截止日期意味着什么？”或者“那么，接下来的一步是什么？”

sentences.en: Some questions are explicitly designed to influence rather than understand.
sentences.zh: 有些问题明显旨在施加影响，而不是为了理解对方。

sentences.en: Leading questions are the most common example.
sentences.zh: 引导性问题就是最典型的例子。

sentences.en: These questions suggest an answer. They suggest a preferred answer.
sentences.zh: 这些问题暗示了一个答案。它们暗示了一个偏好的答案。

sentences.en: Or they maybe include the speaker’s opinion inside the question.
sentences.zh: 或者它们可能把说话者的观点包含在了问题里面。

sentences.en: They often appear in sales or persuasion, media interviews, or police interrogations.
sentences.zh: 它们经常出现在销售、说服、媒体采访或警方审讯中。

sentences.en: “Don’t you think this plan is too risky?”
sentences.zh: “你不觉得这个计划太冒险了吗？”

sentences.en: “Wouldn’t you agree that this is the best option?”
sentences.zh: “难道你不同意这是最好的选择吗？”

sentences.en: Both of those questions have an opinion in them already.
sentences.zh: 这两个问题里面其实都已经包含了一种观点。

sentences.en: “Too risky”. “Best option”. So, the person you are asking the question either has to agree with you or disagree with you.
sentences.zh: “太冒险”。“最好的选择”。所以，被问的人要么得同意你的观点，要么得反对你。

sentences.en: And humans are much more likely to agree than disagree.
sentences.zh: 而人类往往更容易选择同意，而不是反对。

sentences.en: The problem with this type of question is that they are risky.
sentences.zh: 这类问题的问题在于它们带有风险。

sentences.en: People may agree to just avoid conflict, or they may feel manipulated and become defensive.
sentences.zh: 人们可能会为了避免冲突而选择同意，也可能会觉得自己被操控了而产生防御心理。

sentences.en: In everyday conversation, leading questions can limit an honest discussion and they can damage trust.
sentences.zh: 在日常对话中，引导性问题会限制坦诚的讨论，并会破坏信任。

sentences.en: That doesn’t mean they never have a purpose, but in most conversations they should be used very carefully.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着它们毫无用处，但在大多数对话中，应该非常谨慎地使用它们。

sentences.en: There are also questions designed to understand how someone feels or how they see a situation.
sentences.zh: 还有一些问题旨在了解别人的感受或他们如何看待某种情况。

sentences.en: These are often called “affective questions”.
sentences.zh: 这些通常被称为“情感类问题”。

sentences.en: They are extremely important in workplaces or in friendships.
sentences.zh: 它们在职场或友谊中极其重要。

sentences.en: Understanding emotions helps you prevent misunderstandings and builds trust.
sentences.zh: 理解情绪有助于你防止误解并建立信任。

sentences.en: For example: “How do you feel about moving to a new team?”
sentences.zh: 例如：“你对加入一个新团队有什么感觉？”

sentences.en: “Was that change stressful for you?” However, these questions require cultural sensitivity.
sentences.zh: “那个变化对你来说压力大吗？”然而，这些问题需要具备文化敏感性。

sentences.en: In some cultures, talking openly about feelings is normal.
sentences.zh: 在某些文化中，公开谈论感受是很正常的。

sentences.en: In others, it might feel too personal or too inappropriate.
sentences.zh: 而在其他文化中，这可能会让人觉得过于隐私或不太得体。

sentences.en: Good communicators adjust their questions based on context and relationship.
sentences.zh: 优秀的沟通者会根据语境和人际关系来调整他们的提问。

sentences.en: Two useful techniques that combine several question types are funnel questions and iterative questions.
sentences.zh: 有两个结合了多种提问类型的实用技巧，分别是漏斗式提问和迭代式提问。

sentences.en: Funnel questions start broad and gradually become more specific.
sentences.zh: 漏斗式提问由宽泛逐渐变得具体。

sentences.en: They are useful in interviews or in problem solving or in discussions where you are trying to understand a complex situation step by step.
sentences.zh: 它们在面试、解决问题或试图一步步理解复杂情况的讨论中非常有用。

sentences.en: For example, “How has the project been going overall?
sentences.zh: 例如，“整体来说，这个项目进展得怎么样？

sentences.en: Which part has been most challenging? What exactly caused that issue?”
sentences.zh: 哪部分最具挑战性？到底是什么导致了那个问题？”

sentences.en: You are narrowing down on the real topic.
sentences.zh: 你正在一步步锁定真正的话题。

sentences.en: Iterative questions build on previous answers.
sentences.zh: 迭代式提问建立在先前答案的基础之上。

sentences.en: They involve taking an answer and immediately refining it with a follow-up.
sentences.zh: 它们涉及获取一个答案，然后立即通过追问对其进行细化。

sentences.en: You have all probably become quite used to using iterative questions without realizing it.
sentences.zh: 你们大家可能已经在不知不觉中习惯了使用迭代式提问。

sentences.en: This is because we use iterative questions a lot when it comes to working with AI tools.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们在使用AI工具时会大量用到迭代式提问。

sentences.en: For example: “ChatGPT, can you make a summary of this document?
sentences.zh: 例如：“ChatGPT，你能总结一下这份文档吗？

sentences.en: That’s a good summary, but can you explain it as if I were a beginner?
sentences.zh: 总结得不错，但你能用好像我是个初学者的语气解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Can you make it a little bit simpler? Can you add this?
sentences.zh: 能让它简单一点吗？能加上这个吗？

sentences.en: Can you take away this?” This is an iterative question.
sentences.zh: 能把这个去掉吗？”这就是一个迭代式提问。

sentences.en: You get an answer, a response, and you ask another question to improve the answer.
sentences.zh: 你得到了一个答案、一个回应，然后你再问另一个问题来改进这个答案。

sentences.en: At this point, it’s important to be clear about something.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，明确一件事非常重要。

sentences.en: A question can be grammatically correct, but still be a bad question.
sentences.zh: 一个问题在语法上可能是正确的，但它依然可能是一个糟糕的问题。

sentences.en: English learners often focus on technical accuracy.
sentences.zh: 英语学习者往往专注于技术上的准确性。

sentences.en: Focus on the right word order, the correct tense, the correct question form, and of course all of that matters.
sentences.zh: 专注于正确的词序、正确的时态、正确的疑问句形式，当然这些都很重要。

sentences.en: But correctness alone doesn’t make a question “good”.
sentences.zh: 但仅凭正确并不能让一个问题成为“好”问题。

sentences.en: A good question is communicatively effective not just technically correct.
sentences.zh: 一个好问题在沟通上是有效的，而不仅仅是语法正确。

sentences.en: A good question is clear and concise. The listener should immediately understand what you are asking without needing clarification.
sentences.zh: 一个好问题应该清晰简明。听众应该不需要别人解释就能立即听懂你在问什么。

sentences.en: If a question is too long or too complicated, people stop listening.
sentences.zh: 如果一个问题太长、太复杂，人们就不想听了。

sentences.en: They don’t care. Second, a good question has a clear purpose.
sentences.zh: 他们才不在乎呢。其次，一个好问题有明确的目的。

sentences.en: Before you ask it, you should know why you are asking.
sentences.zh: 在你提问之前，你应该知道你为什么要问。

sentences.en: Do you want information? Clarification? A deeper understanding?
sentences.zh: 你是想要信息？澄清疑问？更深入的理解？

sentences.en: To start a conversation? To make a friend?
sentences.zh: 为了开启一段对话？为了交个朋友？

sentences.en: Third, a good question invites a useful or interesting answer.
sentences.zh: 第三，一个好问题能引出有用或有趣的答案。

sentences.en: Fourth, a good question moves the conversation forward.
sentences.zh: 第四，一个好问题能推动对话向前发展。

sentences.en: It adds something. It helps the discussion develop instead of stopping it.
sentences.zh: 它能带来新的内容。它有助于讨论的深入开展，而不是让对话陷入僵局。

sentences.en: And finally, a good question respects the listener’s perspective.
sentences.zh: 最后，一个好问题尊重听者的观点。

sentences.en: It doesn’t assume too much. It doesn’t push an opinion.
sentences.zh: 它不会作过多假设。它不会强加某种观点。

sentences.en: It gives the other person room to answer honestly and in their own way.
sentences.zh: 它给对方留出了空间，让他们能够真诚地、以自己的方式回答。

sentences.en: A technically correct question shows that you know the rules of English.
sentences.zh: 一个语法正确的问题表明你懂英语规则。

sentences.en: A communicatively effective question shows that you understand how English is actually used between people.
sentences.zh: 而一个沟通有效的问题则表明你懂英语在人际交往中是如何真正被使用的。

sentences.en: So how do you actually get better at asking questions?
sentences.zh: 那么，你究竟该如何提高提问水平呢？

sentences.en: Well, here is some advice. The first step is simple… ask more questions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里有一些建议。第一步很简单……多问问题。

sentences.en: Many English learners stay quiet because they’re afraid of making mistakes.
sentences.zh: 许多英语学习者保持沉默是因为他们害怕犯错。

sentences.en: But silence often creates a worse impression than imperfect English.
sentences.zh: 但沉默往往比不完美的英语给人留下更糟糕的印象。

sentences.en: That said, more questions doesn’t mean endless questions.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，多问并不意味着没完没了地问。

sentences.en: Quality matters more than quantity. Good question askers are active and they ask questions because they’re curious.
sentences.zh: 质量比数量更重要。擅长提问的人积极主动，他们因为好奇而提问。

sentences.en: Follow up questions are one of the most powerful tools you have.
sentences.zh: 追问是你拥有的最强有力的工具之一。

sentences.en: They show that you are listening. They show that you care.
sentences.zh: 它们表明你在倾听。它们表明你在乎。

sentences.en: They make conversations feel natural. You don’t need complicated language to ask a good follow-up.
sentences.zh: 它们让对话感觉自然。你不需要复杂的语言就能问出一个好的追问。

sentences.en: Simple things work extremely well. Why? How?
sentences.zh: 简单的东西效果极好。为什么？怎么会这样？

sentences.en: What happened? What happened next? If you want better conversations and more understanding, open questions should be your default.
sentences.zh: 发生什么了？接下来发生了什么？如果你想要更好的对话和更多的理解，开放式问题应该成为你的默认选择。

sentences.en: Open questions invite explanation, reflection, and I guess they help the other person express themselves in their own way.
sentences.zh: 开放式问题能引发解释、反思，我想它们还能帮助对方以自己的方式表达自己。

sentences.en: A very simple example is instead of saying, “do you like cats?”, say, “what is your favorite animal?” Right?
sentences.zh: 一个非常简单的例子是，与其说“你喜欢猫吗？”，不如说“你最喜欢的动物是什么？”对吧？

sentences.en: It’s a very elementary school example, but hopefully you can all understand it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常小学的例子，但希望你们都能听懂。

sentences.en: Instead of saying, “Do you like something?”
sentences.zh: 与其说“你喜欢某个东西吗？”

sentences.en: “Do you want something?” Say, “What would you like?”
sentences.zh: “你想要某个东西吗？”不如说“你想要什么？”

sentences.en: “What do you want?” “How do you do this?”
sentences.zh: “你想要什么？”“你是怎么做这个的？”

sentences.en: There are some clear exceptions, like business decisions or fact checking.
sentences.zh: 有一些明显的例外，比如商业决策或事实核查。

sentences.en: That’s very important. When you need a confirmation or you need a final answer, closed questions are much more effective.
sentences.zh: 这非常重要。当你需要确认或需要一个最终答案时，封闭式问题要有效得多。

sentences.en: You just want a closed “yes” or “no” answer.
sentences.zh: 你只需要一个封闭的“是”或“否”的回答。

sentences.en: One of the easiest ways to improve your questions is to take your opinion out of them.
sentences.zh: 提高提问水平最简单的方法之一，就是把你的主观观点从问题中剔除。

sentences.en: Leading questions limit honest answers. They push people to agree with you or they push people to stay silent, instead of expressing what they really think.
sentences.zh: 引导性问题会限制坦诚的答案。它们会促使人们同意你的观点，或者促使人们保持沉默，而不是表达他们真正的想法。

sentences.en: By using more neutral language, you will probably get better responses and better responses lead to better conversations.
sentences.zh: 通过使用更中立的语言，你可能会得到更好的回应，而更好的回应会带来更好的对话。

sentences.en: If you want useful answers, let the other person do the thinking.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要有用的答案，就让对方去思考吧。

sentences.en: And short questions are usually better questions.
sentences.zh: 而且简短的问题通常是更好的问题。

sentences.en: As a general rule, try to ask a question in one clear sentence.
sentences.zh: 作为一个一般规则，尽量用一个清晰的句子来提出问题。

sentences.en: If you need more explanation, you can always follow up later.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要更多的解释，你随时可以稍后进行追问。

sentences.en: This is especially important in spoken English.
sentences.zh: 这在口语英语中尤为重要。

sentences.en: Spoken language needs to be processed in real time and long questions increase the chance of confusion.
sentences.zh: 口语需要实时处理，冗长的问题会增加产生混淆的几率。

sentences.en: For non-native speakers, shorter questions are also safer.
sentences.zh: 对于非母语者来说，更短的问题也更安全。

sentences.en: They reduce mistakes and they make you sound more confident.
sentences.zh: 它们能减少错误，还能让你听起来更自信。

sentences.en: One important piece of advice you will hear a lot is that great questions start with listening.
sentences.zh: 你经常会听到的一条重要建议是：极好的问题始于倾听。

sentences.en: Listening is an active skill. When people struggle to ask good questions, the real problem is often poor listening.
sentences.zh: 倾听是一项积极的技能。当人们苦于无法提出好问题时，真正的问题往往是倾听能力差。

sentences.en: When you don’t listen carefully, a few things happen.
sentences.zh: 当你没有认真倾听时，就会发生几件事。

sentences.en: You ask questions that have already been answered.
sentences.zh: 你会去问那些已经被回答过的问题。

sentences.en: You miss important details. You create awkward moments where the other person thinks that you were not paying attention.
sentences.zh: 你会错过重要的细节。你会制造出尴尬的时刻，让对方觉得你根本没在注意听。

sentences.en: None of this helps a conversation move forward.
sentences.zh: 这些都无助于推动对话向前发展。

sentences.en: Good listening means letting answers finish even if you think you already know what the person is going to say.
sentences.zh: 良好的倾听意味着让对方把话说完，哪怕你觉得你已经知道对方要说什么了。

sentences.en: It also means resisting the temptation to plan your next question while the other person is still talking.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着克制住那种在别人还在说话时就急着盘算下一个问题的冲动。

sentences.en: Simple nonverbal signals matter. Eye contact, nodding, and small reactions show that you are engaged.
sentences.zh: 简单的非语言信号也很重要。眼神接触、点头以及细微的反应都表明你很投入。

sentences.en: These signals make the other person more comfortable and more willing to continue speaking, at least in a native English speaker context.
sentences.zh: 这些信号会让对方感到更舒适，也更愿意继续说下去，至少在英语母语者的语境中是这样。

sentences.en: I know some cultures don’t necessarily like eye contact or nodding, or have different ways of showing you are engaged.
sentences.zh: 我知道某些文化未必喜欢眼神接触或点头，或者有不同的方式来表达你的投入。

sentences.en: In natural conversations, topics don’t always stay where you expect them to.
sentences.zh: 在自然的对话中，话题并不总是按你预期的方向发展。

sentences.en: Some of the most interesting and useful discussions happen when a conversation moves in an unexpected direction.
sentences.zh: 一些最有趣、最有用的讨论往往发生在对话朝着意料之外的方向发展的时候。

sentences.en: If you are listening properly, you can recognize when it makes sense to follow the new path.
sentences.zh: 如果你倾听得当，你就能识别出什么时候顺着这条新路径走下去是有意义的。

sentences.en: At the same time, there are moments when a conversation needs to be guided or redirected.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，有些时候对话需要被引导或重定向。

sentences.en: Instead of interrupting or disagreeing, you can use questions to bring the focus back.
sentences.zh: 与其打断或表示反对，你可以用问题把焦点拉回来。

sentences.en: Questions that connect the current topic to the original goal and keep the conversation moving.
sentences.zh: 那些能将当前话题与最初目标联系起来并让对话继续推进的问题。

sentences.en: To end this episode, I think we should talk a little bit about AI.
sentences.zh: 在结束这期节目之际，我想我们应该稍微聊聊AI。

sentences.en: Some people worry that AI will reduce the need for communication skills.
sentences.zh: 有些人担心AI会减少对沟通技能的需求。

sentences.en: In reality, it’s kind of done the opposite.
sentences.zh: 现实情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: AI has made the ability to ask clear and good questions more important.
sentences.zh: AI使得提出清晰、好问题的能力变得更加重要。

sentences.en: When you use AI tools, the quality of what you get depends almost entirely on the quality of what you ask.
sentences.zh: 当你使用AI工具时，你获得内容的质量几乎完全取决于你提问的质量。

sentences.en: Vague prompts lead to vague results. When you ask someone a good question, you are clear about your intent.
sentences.zh: 模糊的提示词会导致模糊的结果。当你向某人提出一个好问题时，你的意图是很清晰的。

sentences.en: You give enough context for them to understand the situation, and you apply constraints so that the answer is actually useful.
sentences.zh: 你提供了足够的背景信息让他们理解情况，并且你设定了限制条件，以便答案真正有用。

sentences.en: The same principles apply when prompting AI.
sentences.zh: 提示AI时也是同样的道理。

sentences.en: This means that learning how to ask better questions transfers directly into how effectively you can use AI tools.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，学会提出更好的问题可以直接转化为你使用AI工具的高效程度。

sentences.en: If you are not careful, AI can weaken your curiosity.
sentences.zh: 如果你不够小心，AI可能会削弱你的好奇心。

sentences.en: It becomes easy to stop questioning and to accept the first response and move on.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易停止提问，接受第一个回答然后就此打住。

sentences.en: So your goal should be to use AI as a tool that works with your questions, and that only works if your questions are thoughtful and intentional.​
sentences.zh: 所以你的目标应该是把AI当作一个与你的提问相配合的工具，而这只有在你的提问经过深思熟虑且带有明确意图时才能奏效。

sentences.en: In this episode, I’ve looked at why question asking matters more than ever, what makes a question genuinely good, and how listening, follow up questions, and AI all depend on the same skill… knowing how to ask clear and intentional questions.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我探讨了为什么提问比以往任何时候都重要、什么构成了真正的好问题，以及倾听、追问和AI如何都依赖于同一项技能……那就是知道如何提出清晰且意图明确的问题。

sentences.en: My advice is simple. Start paying attention to the questions you ask.
sentences.zh: 我的建议很简单。开始关注你提出的问题。

sentences.en: Shorten them. Open them up. And don’t be afraid to ask one more follow up.
sentences.zh: 把它们变短。把它们变成开放式。并且不要害怕再多问一个追问。

sentences.en: But what do you think? Do you think you are a “good” question asker?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？你觉得自己是一个“擅长”提问的人吗？

sentences.en: How could you improve? Do you remember a time when you notice someone asking a bad question?
sentences.zh: 你该如何改进？你还记得曾注意到有人提出了一个糟糕问题的时刻吗？
